task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about Dunmere School District's first late-bus service for after-school activities. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Dunmere School District will begin a late-bus service at four secondary schools on Oct. 27, 2026.
The service will run on Tuesdays and Thursdays after district-supervised clubs, study sessions and sports practices.
A one-year $96,000 education-access grant covers the leased bus, driver hours and fuel in the district's approved plan.
The grant does not establish a funded service for subsequent school years.
Students will not pay a fare, but they must register through their school before using a late-bus route.
The bus will use designated neighborhood stops rather than promise a stop at every passenger's home.
School staff will confirm the passenger list before departure and tell families which stop has been assigned.
Transport director Orla Venn said, "An activity can be free to join and still be out of reach if the ride home is missing."
The first route plan links the schools in two collection groups, with departure times adjusted to their different activity schedules.
The district has not published a single districtwide departure time or guaranteed journey duration.
A families group requested a third service day, particularly for activities that meet on Wednesdays.
Families group organizer Teren Moss said, "The two days help, but a club does not move its whole calendar just because a bus is available."
The district will track registrations, actual boardings and unmet requests separately during the first term.
The district has not supplied evidence that the new bus has already increased club participation or improved academic results.
Schools will keep their existing supervision arrangements while registered students wait for the late bus.
Students leaving an unsupervised private activity cannot assume a place on the district service without the required school arrangement.
The contracted driver hours are additional paid hours, not an expectation that existing drivers extend their shifts without compensation.
The district's normal morning and afternoon routes are unchanged by the late-bus grant.
Each participating school will distribute printed registration information as well as electronic notices.
The schools' club lists include gardening, drama, debate and supervised homework sessions, not only competitive teams.
The district will review demand before deciding whether to seek funding for additional days or another bus.
No expansion beyond the four participating schools has been approved.

forbidden_additions: Daily, districtwide or permanently funded service.
Door-to-door travel, an invented common departure time or guaranteed participation gains.
Unpaid driver work or eligibility for any private activity without school arrangements.
preserve: The access benefit alongside limits on days, locations and eligibility.
Registration distinguished from actual boarding and future demand.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
